t.E334.agn: According to EFSA, animal studies showed no toxic effects, including effects on the kidney, and no genotoxic potential. In 2020 EFSA set a group ADI for E 334–337 and E 354 of 240 mg/kg body weight per day, expressed as tartaric acid (replacing the SCF's 1990 ADI of 30 mg/kg), and stated that estimated exposure did not exceed this limit in any age group.
t.E334.body: Absorption of L(+)-tartaric acid is lower in humans than in rats.
t.E334.found.1: Fine bakery wares such as cakes and biscuits
t.E334.prod: Obtained from winemaking residues by chemical processing; its salts are produced by neutralisation.
t.E334.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI for E 334–337 and E 354 of 240 mg/kg body weight per day (as tartaric acid); exposure does not exceed the ADI.
t.E334.regx.1: Removed from Group I by 2024/1451; maximum levels by food category within the 'tartaric acid–tartrates' group (e.g. confectionery 25,000 mg/kg, fine bakery wares 18,000 mg/kg); applies from 16.12.2024.
t.E334.regx.2: ADI 0–30 mg/kg body weight (group ADI for tartaric acid and its sodium, potassium and potassium sodium salts).
t.E334.summary: An acid found naturally in grapes. It gives a sour taste; used in wine, confectionery and baking powder.
t.E334.what: An acid that gives food a sour taste and regulates acidity; it is obtained as a by-product of winemaking.
